html:
SMTO-GWT-0034 — Your message names a different computer than the one selected

GUID: 1d26aaea-8cb6-4ea5-bf86-3aa41d5e6e1e
Slug: gateway-target-ambiguous
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • Your message mentions a computer by name that isn't the one chosen for the request, or mentions several computers when SMTO needed exactly one. SMTO won't guess which you meant, so nothing was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Below the message box, select Show composer controls if they are hidden, then select the Target button and select the computer this request should run on. SMTO follows the computer chosen there and won't let a name in your text switch it silently.
  2. Edit your message so it names only that computer, or remove computer names from it entirely. A different computer name in the text is what made the request unclear.
  3. If you really want several computers, select each of them in Execution target and use Make primary for the main one, then send. Picking several computers in the menu tells SMTO exactly which ones to use.

What success looks like

  • The request starts, and the Via badge or Gateway label on the run shows the computer you intended.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with the computer names in your message. Don't rename a computer just to avoid this; pick the right target instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Legacy prompt routing matched Gateway nicknames in the prompt that conflict with the explicitly selected target, or matched more than one enabled nickname where a single target was required, so no Gateway was chosen.

What this means

  • Legacy prompt routing found named Gateways conflicting with an explicit selection or more than one enabled nickname where a single target was required. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Legacy prompt routing found named Gateways conflicting with an explicit selection or more than one enabled nickname where a single target was required.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare recognized nicknames with the explicit selected target and clarify which machine owns this work.

How to fix it

  • Make the prompt's nickname references agree with the explicit target: select the intended Gateway (or a multi-Gateway selection) in the composer's Execution target menu, or remove the other nicknames from the prompt text. Routing logic is _resolve_legacy_gateway_routing in api/agent_ui_support/gateway.py.
  • Choose the intended Gateway explicitly and make the prompt’s named target consistent with that selection. Do not run against whichever target happens to be available.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Prompt references and explicit routing select the same intended Gateway without ambiguity.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
